reasoning: This is a diagnostic imaging trial comparing 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT to mpMRI for detecting prostate lesions. Step 1 (TARGET ENGAGEMENT): Evidence shows successful detection of PSMA-expressing lesions via PET imaging, indicating the radiotracer bound to its target. Step 2 (PATHWAY MODULATION): The mechanism worked as intended - PSMA binding enabled visualization of lesions. Step 3 (CLINICAL TRANSLATION): The clinical endpoint showed mixed results - 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT detected 24 primary lesions while mpMRI detected 37, suggesting mpMRI was more sensitive for primary lesion detection in this comparison. Step 4 (POPULATION EFFECTS): No subgroup data reported. Step 5 (CONFOUNDERS): Very small sample size (n=20) limits statistical power and generalizability. The trial appears to be a feasibility/comparison study rather than a definitive efficacy trial.
